title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying the Galois action on the 'Fermat tower' over U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,infinity}. He models U_{0,3} as U_1 = {x_0 + x_1 + x_infinity = 0} inside G_m^3/G_m, an open subset of P^2_Q. U_n -> U_1 is the n-th Fermat covering, given by [x_0:x_1:x_infinity] -> [x_0^n : x_1^n : x_infinity^n]. Its total space is the Fermat curve x_0^n + x_1^n + x_infinity^n = 0 with the points where some coordinate vanishes removed.

On the previous page he reduced the homomorphism (329), Pi_Q -> N_sigma^natural = Zhat^* . Zhat, to the Galois action on the fibre of this tower at the rational point '1/2'.

On this page he fixes coordinates for that point: s_{1/2} = (-1/2, -1/2, 1). This is the image of t = 1/2 under t -> (t, 1-t, -1), rescaled; the coordinate sum is 0. It corrects the triple (-1/2, -1/2, -1) written at the bottom of the previous page, whose sum is -2.

Computing the fibre (332):
- A class [x] lies over [a] iff x^n is proportional to a.
- Normalise x_infinity = 1 using the quotient by G_m.
- The fibre then becomes {(x_0, x_1) : x_0^n = -1/2, x_1^n = -1/2}, i.e. T_n(-1/2) x T_n(-1/2).
- Here T_n(xi) (333) is the mu_n-torsor of n-th roots of a unit xi over any base S, here S = Spec Q.

Passing to the limit gives (334): U_infinity(s_{1/2}) = T_infinity(-1/2) x T_infinity(-1/2). Here T_infinity(xi) = lim T_n(xi) (335) is the Kummer torsor of xi under T_infinity(G_m) = Zhat(1).

So the Galois action on the fibre of the Fermat tower at 1/2 is computed by the Kummer character of -1/2 (twice) together with the cyclotomic character. The next page accordingly rewrites (329) via Pi_Q -> Gal(Qtilde[(-1/2)^{1/infinity}]/Q), with Qtilde = Q(mu_infinity). It then opens a general digression on Galois groups of Qtilde[xi_1^{1/infinity}, ..., xi_N^{1/infinity}] over Q, i.e. Kummer theory over the cyclotomic closure, to measure the size of the image in Zhat^* . Zhat.

In modern terms: the abelianised path torsor of P^1 - {0,1,infinity} from a base point to a rational point z is given by the Kummer classes kappa(z) and kappa(1-z). For z = 1/2 both equal kappa(1/2), up to the sign/normalisation coming from -1.
errors: The previous page gives the point as (-1/2,-1/2,-1), which does not satisfy x_0+x_1+x_infinity=0; this page silently corrects it to (-1/2,-1/2,1).
In the first line of (332) the image may show x_infinity^n = -1 rather than 1. It should be 1, or it does not matter after quotienting, since only the ratios x_i^n/x_infinity^n are relevant.

The second line of (332) as transcribed normalises 'x_0 = -1/2'. The correct normalisation is x_infinity = 1, keeping x_0^n = -1/2 and x_1^n = -1/2. This is likely a transcription or handwriting slip.

Subtlety not addressed on this page: Q(mu_8) already contains sqrt(2) and i, hence sqrt(-1/2). So Qtilde((-1/2)^{1/infinity}) has Galois group over Qtilde of index 2 in Zhat(1). The image of Gamma_Q in Zhat^* ⋉ Zhat is therefore not the whole group. Presumably this is what the announced digression on the 'taille' of the image handles.

ideas.what: Fibre of the Fermat tower over P^1-{0,1,infinity} at the rational point 1/2 identified with a product of Kummer torsors T_infinity(-1/2) x T_infinity(-1/2)
ideas.modern_name: Kummer torsor / abelianised (metabelian) path torsor at a rational base point; Galois action on Fermat curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical Kummer theory. Galois action on the Fermat tower: Ihara (1986), Anderson, Coleman, Deligne (1989)

ideas.what: Torsor of n-th roots T_n(xi) of a unit over an arbitrary base and its limit T_infinity(xi) as a T_infinity(G_m)-torsor
ideas.modern_name: Kummer sequence / Tate-module torsor of a unit

ideas.what: Reduction of the image of Pi_Q in Zhat^* . Zhat to Galois groups of Q(mu_infinity)(xi_i^{1/infinity})/Q
ideas.modern_name: Kummer theory over the cyclotomic closure (Bashmakov–Ribet type results)

deep.surprise_reason: A routine explicit computation: the fibre of the Fermat cover at a rational point is a product of Kummer torsors. This is standard and implicit in the Ihara/Anderson/Coleman work on Galois action on Fermat curves. Interest is purely historical, as a worked example in the Longue Marche manuscripts.
transcription_corrections: (332) second line: the normalisation should read x_infinity = 1 (with x_0^n = -1/2, x_1^n = -1/2), not 'x_0 = -1/2'.
(332) first line: the image appears to show x_infinity^n = -1 (possibly a slip for 1).
(333): the struck text reads roughly 'faisceau des racines ... de xi in H^0(S, G_m)'; the replacement is 'torseur des racines n-ièmes de xi'.
In (334) the first factor was overwritten (some sign written then corrected to -1/2); intended T_infinity(-1/2) x T_infinity(-1/2).
